question.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.3$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[5X+4].$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.2+2\cdot 0.25+3\cdot 0.15+4\cdot 0.3 \\  & =2.35.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[5X+4] & =\text{E}[5X]+\text{E}[4] \\  & =5\text{E}[X]+4 \\  & =5\cdot 2.35+4 \\  & =15.75.\end{aligned}
$$
